title: Dense model on four GPUs: four copies, two pairs, or one wide server
design_ref: Parallelism: tensor parallelism trades per-GPU efficiency for memory; replicas trade memory for independence
purpose: Serve one 4B model on the same four GPUs three ways (4 x TP1, 2 x TP2, 1 x TP4), predict the KV cache each leaves, and compare goodput per GPU on identical traffic.

checks.description: tp1x4: every server starts and answers its health check
tp2x2: every server starts and answers its health check
tp4x1: every server starts and answers its health check
the KV memory per GPU follows the sharding arithmetic within 8% for every layout
checks.because: Weights are split over the group, so each GPU keeps (1 - 1/n) of the weight size for cache. Largest difference 2.3% (the engine also reserves a little more for activations and communication buffers as groups widen).

checks.description: a wider tensor-parallel group holds more tokens in total: 1 x TP4 > 2 x TP2 > 4 x TP1
checks.because: Total KV tokens 127,104 (4 x TP1), 234,528 (2 x TP2), 285,536 (1 x TP4). Four copies of the weights waste 3 x 7.6 GiB that one sharded copy gives back to the cache.

checks.description: every layout has a measured capacity: some load level kept 95% of requests inside their targets
checks.because: A layout whose lightest level already fails would be reporting the targets, not the layout.

notes: PREDICTED goodput per GPU, best to worst: tp1x4 > tp2x2 > tp4x1 (a 4B model fits on one T4; extra communication over PCIe buys nothing the model needs). MEASURED: tp4x1 > tp2x2 > tp1x4. The prediction did not hold; see the numbers above for which effect won (memory freed for cache, or decode reading half the weights per GPU).

Lightest-load latency: chat ITL p95 47 ms (TP1), 32 ms (TP2), 47 ms (TP4). Decode is limited by reading the weights from memory each step; a wider group reads less per GPU and adds an all-reduce over PCIe per layer.
